name: p_additive_eff
source: No enteric-methane credit in the central case because the area-scaled cattle count is not disaggregated into animals covered by the current EU 3-NOP authorisation. Sensitivities include 30% 3-NOP efficacy on 70% of cattle-days and 80% Asparagopsis efficacy.

name: p_slurry_collect
source: Project design requirement: all collectable pig slurry is routed promptly to the central anaerobic-digestion facility

name: p_cattle_manure_collect
source: Collectable/housed cattle-manure share; all manure in this share is routed to the central digester; pasture manure remains outside the collection boundary

name: p_digest_avoid
unit: fraction of routed-manure storage CH4 avoided
source: Central high-quality gas-tight digester assumption; approximately the reduction implied by IPCC 2019 high-productivity anaerobic-digestion factors versus long-retention liquid/slurry storage in cool climates; sensitivity 0.80–0.95

name: p_cattle_vs
source: IPCC 2006 Tier 1, Western Europe other cattle

name: p_leak
source: Central 3% additional methane loss for upgrading, compression and piping beyond the digester-management factor; sensitivity 1–6%. Together with residual managed-manure methane, this gives a central managed-manure/biomethane-chain methane residual of about 5.8% of gross methane production, close to the 5.4% mean measured across 31 European biogas plants by Olczak et al. (2026).

name: p_pig_slurry_t_head_yr
source: Screening midpoint of 1.1–1.5 m3/head-yr for finisher pig slurry in European/Spanish BAT literature; density approximated as 1 t/m3

name: p_cattle_manure_t_head_yr
